items: No handler, no atexit, no destructors
No flush — buffered writes are simply lost
Temp files, lock files, shm segments left behind

blocks.title: Not A Shortcut
blocks.text: kill -9 first is the mistake, not the fast path. Send TERM, wait the grace period, escalate only if the process is still there.

items: A D-state task cannot be killed immediately
The kill is marked pending in the task
It lands once the task leaves the kernel
A wedged driver can hold it there forever

lines: CMD ["myapp"]        # exec form, app is PID 1
# CMD myapp          # sh is PID 1, eats TERM
# or in a script:  exec myapp

caption.text: Part 3 of LINUX PROCESSES & SIGNALS. kill -9 didn't work? The process was in D state, sitting inside the kernel, not reading signals until its disk I/O returned. 14 pages of handwritten notes on how Linux really creates, runs and kills processes: fork returning twice, exec never returning, the zombie you cannot kill, why your container takes exactly 10 seconds to stop, and the full signal catalog. Save it for the next time a daemon won't die.
